adopt.pattern: Price, latency and a quality score on every picker row, plus one-click presets and a stage-coloured headline bar (VP version: INR, measured on Indian lines, includes telephony and the turn wait)
adopt.evidence: wt-vapi-14/20, files 51-voice-model-dropdown.png, 33-riley-assistant.png (O); walkthrough s13 lists it as best-in-class across 6 dashboards
adopt.why: Lets a self-serve buyer choose a stack (decision.2026-10-20.product-stack-selectable) without reading docs; Vapi's own headline understates (1,530 ms vs our 2.32 s demo p50), so adopt the pattern and fix the honesty.

adopt.pattern: Immutable agent versions with hash and parent, pinned by label, plus a traffic split between versions
adopt.why: Parity floor confirmed at 4 of 5 incumbent APIs; needed for safe change and for v2 guarded ramping.

adopt.pattern: Typed per-component cost lines on every call (transport, transcriber, model, voice, platform, analysis) plus an analytics query endpoint
adopt.why: Enables cost per call and per campaign; extend with contact and campaign group-bys that Vapi lacks.

adopt.pattern: Per-turn latency (model, voice, transcriber, endpointing, turn) stored in the call record, and latency assertions inside simulations
adopt.why: Makes the reply gap a first-class, testable quantity; VP adds handset-side clocks because Vapi's are server-side.

adopt.pattern: Webhook envelope with call-changing request/response events (assistant-request, tool-calls, transfer destination, campaign.predial veto)
adopt.evidence: AP-28/30 (O); the predial veto is the only pre-dial hook in 5 APIs (account SYNTHESIS)
adopt.why: Lets customers inject CRM context and suppression; VP ships it slimmer, signed and with retries by default.

adopt.pattern: QA chain: structured outputs feed scorecards; simulation personalities x scenarios with evaluations and latency expectations; GitOps path fields
adopt.evidence: AP-16/17/61 (O); 51 of 143 public operations are QA (XS-37)
adopt.why: A programmable QA layer is table stakes for enterprise buyers and the substrate for self-learning.

adopt.pattern: Monitoring with severity, MTTR, calls impacted and categories including Compliance; free default monitors offered up front
adopt.why: Good model for an issue inbox; fix the empty-state lie ('Great news' with zero monitors).

adopt.pattern: Grouped tool catalogue (phone-call tools, assistant tools, integrations) and describe-or-pick agent creation with a Composer-style chat entry in every header
adopt.why: Fast path to a first agent in 3 steps; chat setup is parity in 5 of 6 dashboards, so VP wins on result, not on having it.

adopt.pattern: Empty states that explain the concept and offer one action; gated features shown in place with their tier
adopt.why: Teaches the product while empty; avoid the action-less crown card.

adopt.pattern: Provider catalogue breadth (14 STT, 17 LLM, 20 voice variants) with BYOK, fallback voices and transcribers, config-as-code and generated TS/Python SDKs plus MCP
adopt.why: Developer-surface floor; VP curates defaults on top and exposes every dashboard action on API and MCP.

beat.gap: No contact object: customer is inline on every call and campaign row; no consent, DND/NCPR, suppression or attempt history; the only pre-dial hook needs the buyer's own scrub list.
beat.how_vp_beats: First-class Contact with India-default E.164, consent source, DND status and attempt history; predial veto ON by default against VP's own scrub list. Test: messy 50-row synthetic CSV (empty number, 10-digit numbers, duplicates, an opt-out row, Devanagari names) scored for correct rows in under 5 min and zero dials to the opt-out row, against Vapi's server-side outcome (must check the server, not the dashboard code).
beat.evidence: VAP-02/47/49, AP-12/58 (O); wt-vapi-43 (O); 0 of 6 dashboards put consent/DND/DLT on the campaign form (walkthrough s0 finding 1)

beat.gap: Campaign windows are one absolute range per campaign with no recurring daily window, no per-contact timezone, no retry; unanswered contacts are dropped at latestAt; outage calls were not retried.
beat.how_vp_beats: Recurring daily windows in 09:00-21:00 IST style, per-contact local time, retry policy with attempt budgets and backoff, resume after outage. Test: 3-day 10:00-21:00 IST schedule in one campaign, count of contacts retried per policy, and a forced-failure drill that resumes without human action.

beat.gap: Native telephony cannot present an Indian or declared CLI (no 140xx/1600xx, no DLT or A2P path); buyer needs a second vendor account and a +1 caller ID; no India region.
beat.how_vp_beats: Indian-line path with series CLI, A2P declaration and KYC walkthrough shown before the campaign wizard. Test: minutes from sign-up to the first ring on an Indian handset from an Indian CLI, against Vapi's at least 45 min with a +1 CLI (VAP-P02).
beat.evidence: VAP-42/43/44/48 (O/I); wt-vapi-41, 06c-free-vapi-number.png (O); W7 untested on both sides

beat.gap: Reply gap on Indian phone lines: US-West orchestration plus an international Twilio leg; demo p50 2.32 s from US-East; defaults hide the 1.5 s wait; collisions 35%.
beat.how_vp_beats: India-hosted media and orchestration with a published, handset-side measured reply gap. Test: stereo-recorded battery, at least 30 clean turns per vendor, pass if VP p50 is at least 0.3 s below Vapi, p90 2.5 s or less, collisions under Vapi's 35% (hypothesis W3, unproven until run; VP's own lab still shows 15-42% cut-ins).
beat.evidence: M: l4b report (n=40, p50 2.32 s, 25/72 collisions); VAP-20, wt-vapi-12/19; open.2026-10-19.turn-taking

beat.gap: Hinglish is configuration with English-first defaults: 22 English acknowledgement and 20 English interruption phrases, English-only smart endpointing, no phrase lists in the dashboard, no Indian speech vendor, Indic picker narrower than the API, 2 'Indian American' voices; demo replied in Gujarati on 17/18 Hinglish turns.
beat.how_vp_beats: Hinglish as the default mode with editable Hindi backchannel and interruption lists (haan, achha, theek hai, nahi, ruko), a language lock, never-discard-short-reply policy, all Indian languages in the picker and voices filtered by language and region. Test: per-turn language ID on the Hinglish and elderly-Hindi battery, pass at 95% or more correct language and short replies ('haan') never dropped.

beat.gap: Outcomes are 638 engineering codes keyed to providers; the dashboard shows a truncated code; no business outcome; /analytics cannot group by campaign or contact.
beat.how_vp_beats: Business-language outcome and suggested action beside the raw carrier code; cost per contact and per campaign. Test: find a failed call and read its reason and next action in under 60 s (Vapi: found within 5 min but code only, VAP-P07).

beat.gap: State integrity: a menu click creates and publishes a tool, a dropdown autosaves a draft, the Draft label lies after Discard, API PATCH publishes while the dashboard drafts, Next disabled with no reason.
beat.how_vp_beats: One publish path (draft, test, publish, ramp) where nothing is created or saved by a menu click, an always-correct unsaved marker, a materialised resolved-config view of what will actually run, and a reason plus fix link beside every disabled primary action. Test: click-through audit of every create menu and dropdown for server writes; zero unexpected writes.

beat.gap: Headline numbers are component sums that leave out telephony and the turn wait (1,530 ms; USD 0.09), USD-only billing, no per-number price, no GST field.
beat.how_vp_beats: One all-in INR per minute headline including telephony, pulse and the turn wait, with measured India p50/p90 beside any vendor figure. Test: T7 billing audit, 10 calls at 30, 45 and 90 s; invoice within 2% of the headline.
beat.evidence: wt-vapi-12/13/19/45 (I/O); account SYNTHESIS price table (Vapi INR 12.5-17.0 via Twilio vs VP target about INR 2)

beat.gap: Chat-driven setup (Composer) has no REST surface and the MCP server covers only 4 resource families; org, billing and spend cap need a dashboard session; webhooks carry the whole assistant and call on every event with no retry by default.
beat.how_vp_beats: Every dashboard and chat action is an API and MCP operation with the same auth, including spend cap and concurrency; slim signed webhooks with replay. Test: an agent can set up, launch and read back a campaign end to end through API only.

beat.gap: No cross-call memory for voice and a manual learning loop (monitors, issues, evals, simulations, manual splits); Composer-under-Bypass and Mission Control are human-started or flag-gated.
beat.how_vp_beats: v2: per-customer memory store, personalisation and guarded automatic ramping against guardrail metrics (cut-in rate, reply gap, opt-out), learning from outcomes with safety by predicate. Test (v2, not yet built): second-call continuity score on a synthetic customer set, and a ramp that auto-halts on a guardrail breach. Do not claim Vapi cannot auto-improve.
beat.evidence: AP-22/51, VAP-60/61 (O/I); l6 bandit work; ledger.LRN-09
